## Removing entries without official grade reported

```{r Cleaning data}
# to download the full 68MB dataset, you can use:
smarvus_raw <- read_csv("https://osf.io/download/a4zmv/")

### This bit can be replaced with saba's cleaned df once ready
# ============================================================
# Identifying names of no grade recorded
unique(smarvus_raw$grade)

# Remove participants with no reportes Grade Data
smarvus_raw <- smarvus_raw |>
  filter(!grade %in% c(
    "Not Available", 
    NA, 
    "Non complete - LoA", 
    "No stats module on record", 
    "No stats modules", 
    "No access to transcript",
    "-"
  ))
# ============================================================

# Prints all the ways people have inputed the grade
unique(smarvus_raw$grade)

# Prints all the grade conversions
unique(smarvus_raw$grade_category_notes)

# Making easy to read reference df
smarvus_grades_only <- data.frame(
  survey_id = smarvus_raw$survey_id,
  grade = smarvus_raw$grade,
  grade_catagory_notes = smarvus_raw$grade_category_notes
)
smarvus_grades_only
```

```{r Defining grade bands}
# In all cases grade assigned is by taking the mid point of the grade band

# ==================================
# brawijaya conversion
# "A > 80, 75 < B+ ≤ 80, 69 < B ≤ 75, 60 < C+ ≤ 69, 55 < C ≤ 60, 50 < D+ ≤ 55, 44 < D ≤ 50, E < 44"     
brawijaya_conversion <- c(
  "A"  = 90,
  "B+" = 77.5, "B"  = 72,
  "C+" = 64.5, "C"  = 57.5,
  "D+" = 52.5,"D"  = 47,
  "E"  = 22     
)
# ==================================
# hungary conversion
# **No info given**
# found from University of Debrecen, https://eng.unideb.hu/en/grading-system-hungary-university-debrecen 
hungary_conversion <- c(
  "5" = 95,
  "4" = 84.5,
  "3" = 74.5,
  "2" = 64.5,
  "1" = 29.5
)

# ==================================
# la_laguna
# **No info given**

# ==================================
# limerik
# taking the mid point of the grade band
# ">80 = A1, 75-79 = A2, 70-74 = B1, 65-69 = B2, 60-64 = B3, 55-59 = C1, 50-54 = C2, 45-49 = C3,
# 40-44 = D1, 35-39 = D2, <35 = F
limerick_conversion <- c(
  "A1"  = 90, "A2" = 77, 
  "B1"  = 73, "B2" = 67, "B3" = 62,
  "C1" = 57, "C2"  = 52, "C3" = 47,
  "D1" = 42, "D2"  = 37,
  "F"  = 17.5     
)

# ==================================
# mef
# taking the mid point of the grade band
# "A = 90-100, A- = 80-89, B+ = 75-79, B = 70-74, B- = 65-69; C+ = 60-64, C = 55-59, C- = 50-54, 
# D+ = 45-49, D = 35-44, F <35"   
mef_conversion <- c(
  "A"  = 95, "A-" = 84.5, 
  "B+"  = 77, "B" = 72, "B-" = 67,
  "C+" = 62, "C"  = 57, "C-" = 52,
  "D+" = 47, "D"  = 39.5,
  "F"  = 17.5     
)

# ==================================
# rotterdam 
# **No info given**

# ==================================
# uc_louvain
# **No info given**

# ==================================
# vienna
# **No info given**

# york_can
# **No info given**
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

```{r Standardising grades in df}
# Standardizing grades to be out of 100 (eg 98.10 or 36.75)
standardise_grade <- function(df) {df %>%
  mutate(
    grade = as.character(grade),
    grade_std = case_when(
      # anglia_ruskin and sussex: Grades with "%" in them
      survey_id %in% c("anglia_ruskin", "sussex") ~
        suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("%", "", grade))),

      # brawijaya conversion
      survey_id %in% "brawijaya" ~
        unname(brawijaya_conversion[grade]),
      
      # hungary conversion
      survey_id %in% "hungary" ~
        unname(hungary_conversion[grade]),
      
      # la_laguna
      # update once found reputable conversion
      
      # limerick
      survey_id %in% "limerick" ~
        unname(limerick_conversion[grade]),
      
      # mef
      survey_id %in% "mef" ~
        unname(mef_conversion[grade]),  
      
      # rotterdam 
      # update once found reputable conversion

      # uc_louvain
      # update once found reputable conversion
      
      # vienna
      # update once found reputable conversion
      
      # york_can
      # update once found reputable conversion

    )
  )
}

# Once got saba's final cleaned code run it through the function
# ================================================================
final_standardised_grade <- standardise_grade(smarvus_grades_only)
# ================================================================

```
